dominant_breach: leveraged healthcare ownership can extract hospital assets and cash flows while patients, workers, municipalities, and state agencies inherit continuity-of-care and public-health backstop risk
fastest_washout: service-line cuts, closure, emergency transition, workforce loss, Medicaid/Medicare/public-health spillovers, and local travel burdens wash out any nominal efficiency gains

public_balance_sheet_gate.note: Hospital financialization becomes a public-balance-sheet case when essential-care continuity is implicitly guaranteed while private sponsors, landlords, lenders, or related parties have already extracted cash flow or assets.

healthcare_financialization_public_backs.note: Private equity and consolidation evidence now supports active scoring of continuity-of-care risk, public transition cost, and extraction-before-rescue dynamics.

hospital_sale_leaseback_asset_stripping_.note: Sale-leaseback, dividend, fee, debt, and asset-transfer structures must be mapped as senior claims on hospital cash flow before public rescue terms are assessed.

essential_service_closure_public_cost.note: Closure, transition, travel, EMS, workforce, and service-line continuity costs must be booked as public exposure, not treated as private-business failure alone.

healthcare_transaction_ownership_transpa.note: Ownership/control and related-party transparency must precede transaction approval or public support; otherwise the rescue target and extraction beneficiaries are obscured.

health_medical_debt_drag.note: Market consolidation and degraded access can interact with household medical-debt and cost burdens even when the case begins as an ownership/continuity problem.

place_public_finance_gate.note: A hospital is a place-based public-service floor; closure converts corporate distress into community wealth and service-wealth loss.

public_service_floor_place_equality.note: Loss of nearby hospital capacity undermines the local service floor and can force claimants into travel, delay, or emergency-system displacement.

enforceability_and_remedy_access.note: Remedies require review authority, capital-maintenance covenants, service-line protections, and clawbacks before extraction occurs.

proof_debt: hospital ownership/control chain, debt, management fee, dividend, sale-leaseback, and related-party transaction map
capital-maintenance, staffing, charity-care, service-line, quality, and access covenant audit
closure/transition public-cost ledger across Medicaid/Medicare, state health agencies, municipalities, workers, and patients
lender/landlord/sponsor seniority versus patient/community continuity seniority under distress
clawback, escrow, lien, certificate-of-need, transaction-review, and public-interest covenant enforcement tools

gate_08_liability_stack_life_interruptio.why: Health-care interruption is an immediate life-interruption channel.

gate_11_enforceability_remedies.why: Remedy access depends on transaction review, ownership transparency, and enforceable service/capital covenants.

gate_15_place_public_finance.why: Hospital continuity is a local service-wealth floor.

gate_20_public_balance_sheet.why: Comfort certification is blocked until ownership/control, asset-stripping, closure-transition cost, patient/community seniority, and clawback/public-interest covenant terms are enforceable.

evidence_debt_register.question: ownership/control and related-party transaction map
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Attach ownership, MPT/landlord, lender, management-fee, dividend, debt, and sale-leaseback details before public support or closure certification.

evidence_debt_register.question: continuity-of-care public cost ledger
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Quantify EMS, Medicaid/Medicare, state transition, travel-time, workforce, and service-line replacement costs.

evidence_debt_register.question: public recovery from prior extraction beneficiaries
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Test clawbacks, escrows, liens, transaction-review conditions, certificate-of-need penalties, and public-interest covenants.

validation_notes: rev0320 treats essential-care continuity as a public-balance-sheet exposure when private financial engineering makes the public sector the de facto guarantor.

rev0327 promotes this scoreboard to active: the evidence supports public-backstop scoring of ownership/control, extraction, closure-transition costs, and public recovery, even though transaction-level ledgers remain proof debt.

20A_debt_interest_capacity.question: Do debt service and maturity/interest risks crowd out floors, services, enforcement, public investment, or countercyclical repair?
20A_debt_interest_capacity.finding: This subgate is not a material live channel in this case.

20B_claim_security.question: Are social-insurance, pension, health, disability, care, or public-benefit promises financed and legally durable enough to count as wealth substitutes?
20B_claim_security.finding: Health-care access functions as a public claim; private extraction can degrade claim security before public rescue activates.

20C_contingent_liabilities_guarantees.question: Are guarantees, insurance funds, credit programs, SOEs, PPPs, disaster obligations, and legal claims disclosed and stress-tested?
20C_contingent_liabilities_guarantees.finding: State agencies and public payers become contingent continuity guarantors when essential hospitals fail.

20D_crisis_backstop_governance.question: Who is rescued under stress, under what terms, with what haircut, condition, sunset, and report?
20D_crisis_backstop_governance.finding: Closure/transition decisions reveal who is protected first: lenders/landlords/sponsors or patients, workers, and communities.

20E_public_upside_recovery.question: Does the public receive warrants, equity, fees, clawbacks, senior claims, recoveries, or other upside when it absorbs downside?
20E_public_upside_recovery.finding: Public rescue and transition aid need clawbacks, liens, escrow, or public-interest covenants against prior extraction beneficiaries.

20F_central_bank_quasi_fiscal_visibility.question: Are remittance losses, deferred assets, interest-on-reserves distribution, facilities, and asset-price stabilization effects visible?
20F_central_bank_quasi_fiscal_visibility.finding: This subgate is not a material live channel in this case.

20G_public_asset_sovereign_wealth_govern.question: Are public assets rule-bound, professionally managed, protected from raiding, and linked to ordinary claimants?
20G_public_asset_sovereign_wealth_govern.finding: This subgate is not a material live channel in this case.

20H_generational_intergovernmental_incid.question: Does repair fall on younger cohorts, renters, disabled claimants, caregivers, migrants, municipalities, or future taxpayers?
20H_generational_intergovernmental_incid.finding: Local governments, state health agencies, public payers, and future patients inherit service-floor repair costs.

public_balance_sheet_register.legal_authority: State health transaction review, certificate-of-need and licensure authority, Medicaid/Medicare payment, public-health emergency authority, attorney general charity/consumer protection powers, bankruptcy/receivership tools, and public transition funding.
public_balance_sheet_register.claimant_perimeter: Patients, workers, emergency-service networks, public payers, local governments, hospital creditors, landlords/REITs, private-equity sponsors, and acquiring systems
public_balance_sheet_register.maximum_exposure: Unknown without hospital-system financial and closure registers; includes transition aid, uncompensated care shifts, emergency routing, workforce dislocation, and public-health capacity losses
public_balance_sheet_register.expected_loss: Case-specific; expected loss rises when debt, rent, management fees, and deferred capital maintenance outrun operating cash flow and public transition options are slow
public_balance_sheet_register.stress_scenario: A financially engineered hospital operator cuts staffing or services, defaults, sells assets, or closes; state agencies and public payers must preserve emergency and community health access while creditors, landlords, and sponsors assert senior private claims.
public_balance_sheet_register.funding_source: public payer payments, state/municipal transition support, emergency-service budgets, uncompensated-care pools, acquiring-system subsidies, philanthropy, and patient household costs
public_balance_sheet_register.loss_sharing: Sponsors, landlords, lenders, management-fee recipients, and dividend/asset-transfer beneficiaries should face clawback, escrow, lien, covenant, or subordination before public continuity funds are used.
public_balance_sheet_register.public_upside_recovery: Public-interest covenants, senior public liens, transaction-approval conditions, clawbacks, escrowed capital maintenance, community benefit obligations, and service-line continuity penalties.
public_balance_sheet_register.ordinary_claimant_protection: Patients, workers, rural/low-income communities, disabled claimants, and emergency-care users must be senior to sponsor/landlord fee and dividend claims during rescue
public_balance_sheet_register.sunset_or_review: Annual healthcare-transaction review and event-triggered refresh after bankruptcy, closure, receivership, service-line loss, or public transition funding.
